issues.on_page: Special Revenue - Keno Fund, Statement of Gross Proceeds Distribution: Gross proceeds 439,865; Declared prizes (333,105); Lottery Operator's Commission (61,580); State taxes (8,797); Other expenses (711); Transfers to prize reserves 2,016; Community betterment projects (22,406); Interest income 404
issues.issue: The Keno Fund schedule has no detail lines, but every other fund's schedule (pp6-13, 17-18) is in detail. Leaving it out is deliberate: the schedule shows gross proceeds, and the fund statement's Keno income of 37,688 is the net figure (45,180 - 9,508 + 2,016). FY2023-FY2025 also leave it out. Statement totals are not affected.

issues.on_page: Cash and Equivalents 1,184,425; Restricted cash and equivalents 756,247 (Total column)
issues.issue: ending_cash includes only unrestricted Cash and Equivalents. Restricted cash of 756,247 (Debt Service 539,759 + Keno 216,488) is also printed as cash but is left out of the cash measure. FY2023 has the same open question: which cash measure is wanted?

General Fund 'Fireworks' receipts are kept as other. In a village these are usually fireworks sales permit/license fees (licenses and permits), but the page does not say so. It is a judgment call. The same applies to detail[9].

Street Fund 'Incentive pay' is probably the state street superintendent incentive payment (state aid), but no grantor is printed. Keeping it as other follows the 2026-11-12 ruling. The same applies to detail[89].

The printed amount is negative: a loss on disposal (the cash flow statement shows sale proceeds of 5,500, and the Statement of Activities counts the 1,145 in Sewer expenses of 294,459). The 2026-11-06 Scottsbluff ruling puts such a loss in category 'Loss on Disposal of Assets'. Recording it as a negative Sale of Property receipt can be defended, but the category is questionable. The same applies to detail[163].
